endorsements.quote: It is our view that AI should not, however, be the final decision maker.
In high-stakes environments, it is important for AI algorithms to predict not only their target (a measurement, a class, a segmentation), but also the con fidence in its prediction 65.
We argue that in many POCUS applications, it is possible to have an interpretable prediction, even if the system relies on the use of “black box” models during the intermediate stages.

unlisted_practices: Developers should allow AI systems to return 'unable to predict' for borderline cases, poor image quality, or out-of-distribution inputs rather than give a misleading answer.
Developers should take extra steps to calibrate AI predictors, such as Platt scaling, isotonic regression, or temperature parameters.
Developers should design AI to output intermediate results, such as segmentations, landmarks, and measurements, that clinicians can visually verify and edit.
Developers should include images acquired by users of different experience levels, devices, and imaging conditions in training data.
Developers should train POCUS AI models on ultrasound data, ideally acquired with POCUS devices, rather than relying on models pretrained on natural images.
Developers should apply domain adaptation techniques such as style transfer to reduce performance loss across devices and settings.
Developers should involve all stakeholders regularly in AI development and deployment, including user feedback to detect bias.
Developers should test whether demographic attributes can be identified from images to decide which subpopulations need sufficient training samples.
Developers should ensure AI learns representations invariant to confounding variables such as sex and race, avoiding shortcut learning.
